messages:
maria.g: Heads up — getting multiple customer escalations in support about hosted API returning 5xx and timeouts since ~08:42 UTC. SLO alert firing. Anyone already looking?
ben.k: seeing the same on dashboards, spike in 5xx from api-gateway-ingress cluster starting 08:41. SLO burn = 3.6% over 10m.
chris_p: digging traces now. A lot of traces end with auth-service returning 401 and then gateway throwing 502/504-ish upstream errors. Looks like the gateway is surfacing as 5xx instead of mapping to 4xx.
elaine: support reported billing auth failures for a subset of customers at the same time — tokens failing refresh calls. Might be related.
sre-bot: Alert: SLO_BURN: hosted-api-p95-latency exceeded threshold. Count=1247, Window=10m.
ben.k: quick query I ran in logs (CloudLogging):
```
logName="projects/redwood-prod/logs/gateway" severity>=ERROR
resource.labels.cluster_name="api-gateway-ingress"
timestamp>="2026-03-12T08:35:00Z"
jsonPayload.status_code: (502 OR 504 OR 500)
| top 50
```
Shows a bunch of upstream errors from `auth-service:443` and `billing-service:8443` timeouts.
maria.g: can someone grep for `token_refresh` and `connection reset by peer` in the timeframe?
chris_p: already: `token_refresh` failures correlate with `upstream_connect_timeout` in envoy. Sample trace: request->gateway->auth-service (grpc)/timeout->gateway returns 502. Full trace has no downstream child spans after auth call — trace gap there. Possibly auth-service crash or overloaded.
elaine: support repro steps: 1) POST /v1/generate with valid api key 2) immediately get 502/504 in ~30-60s 3) curl to /health on auth-service returns 200 at times, but token refresh endpoints intermittently 5xx.
ben.k: hypothesize: auth-service hitting KMS for token signing, KMS region had elevated latency -> causes auth-service RPCs to stall -> gateway hits its timeout and surfaces 5xx. We should verify KMS and billing downstream metrics.
maria.g: good hypothesis. Ben, can you check KMS latency graph and KMS error rate around 08:40?
ben.k: KMS in eu-west-1 had a short spike in RPC latency at 08:39-08:44 with increased retries. Also saw elevated 503s from billing-calls to external payments gateway at same interval. Two concurrent downstream degradations could push auth-service over its timeout budget.
chris_p: mitigation idea: change gateway behavior to map auth-service 401/403 to 401 upstream rather than turning into 5xx when timeout? Also extend auth-service retry/backoff to avoid hammering KMS during its transient.
elaine: from support side, suggested temporary customer-facing mitigation: set retry header to reduce client retries, enable fallback model (lighter) for affected customers. But we need infra fix first.
sre-bot: Incident channel created: #incident/2187654321. Priority: P2.
maria.g: TODOs: 1) Short-term hotfix: tweak gateway to treat upstream auth errors as 4xx where possible and increase upstream timeout for auth-service to 8s (currently 3s). 2) Add circuit breaker on auth-service to return 503 quickly if overloaded. 3) Longer: investigate KMS dependency and add async token refresh cache.
ben.k: applying temporary routing change to ingress config now. Command: `kubectl -n ingress apply -f ingress-auth-timeout-patch.yaml` patch contains:
```
- upstream: auth-service:443
  timeout: 8s
  retry: 1
  status_mapping:
    401: 401
    403: 403
```
deploy-bot: deploy started: ingress/patch (rollout id: r-20260312-01)
chris_p: while that's rolling, I'm adding a PromQL alert for `upstream_connect_timeout` spikes and a log-based metric for `token_refresh` failures so we get earlier signal. Query suggestion: `sum(rate(envoy_cluster_upstream_cx_connect_fail{cluster="auth-service"}[1m])) by (instance)`
maria.g: also add a TraceQL quick query to capture traces that end at auth-service with no downstream spans so we can estimate how many requests lost child spans.
elaine: support update to customers: "We're aware of intermittent timeouts impacting inference requests and are applying mitigations. If you see errors, retry after 60s. We're tracking this as priority and will update in 30m." :thumbsup:
ben.k: ingress patch finished. Observability shows 5xx rate dropping within 2 minutes. SLO burn down to 1.1% but still above alert threshold.
chris_p: traced a sample where auth-service returned 500 because it blocked waiting on KMS sign call — stacktrace shows call stack waiting on external KMS client.
maria.g: confirm adding the circuit breaker on auth-service. Ben, can you roll a patch to auth-service to short-circuit token issuance when queue depth > 200 and return a 429/503 quickly? That will be safer than letting downstream cascade.
ben.k: I'll open PR and roll canary to one replica. PR: `auth-service: add cb for token refresh (queue depth)`.
chris_p: added quick Grafana panel with token_refresh latency distribution and KMS RPC latency. Link: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abcd/auth-timeouts (paste in incident channel)
sre-bot: Reminder: add postmortem owner and start timeline in #postmortems when incident stabilizes.
maria.g: agreed. Assigning postmortem to @maria.g and @chris_p. Once immediate mitigations are in prod and SLO < 0.5% for 30m, we'll close incident.
elaine: support will collect affected customer list and examples for SEs. Also grab request ids from logs for customers who opened tickets.
ben.k: can confirm initial root cause: transient KMS latency + payment gateway degradation led to auth-service overload -> upstream timeouts -> gateway 5xx/timeout SLO burn. Mitigations applied: ingress timeout increase, status mapping, auth-service circuit breaker canary.
maria.g: notes for postmortem: include reproducible query snippets, e.g., CloudLogging queries used, PromQL rules added, and the ingress patch diff. Also include a load replay to reproduce auth-service KMS latency coupling.
chris_p: example CloudLogging snippet for timeline:
```
resource.type="k8s_container"
labels.k8s-pod/app="auth-service"
textPayload:"token_refresh"
timestamp>="2026-03-12T08:30:00Z" AND timestamp<="2026-03-12T09:00:00Z"
```
maria.g: closing loop — monitoring shows SLO back to target at 08:58. Will keep watch and update postmortem later. Thanks all. :heart:
